title: Existential phase search
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, let $K(j)$ be a proposition for each natural number $j$, and let $σ=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ be a program register state. Suppose every register of $σ$ is at most $B$, $s=0$, $tmp=0$, and $p+2n+2\le B$. Assume that for every $j<n$, if the binary word of $j$ is doubled at position $p$ in $x$, then the program started at the target stage with source register $j$, pointer $p+2|\mathrm{bits}(j)|+2$, and scratch register zero terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when $K(j)$ holds. Then the program started at the existential-search stage in state $σ$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when there exists $j<n$ for which the binary word of $j$ is doubled at position $p$ in $x$ and $K(j)$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: $K$ is a predicate on natural numbers
all nine registers of $\u001bσ$ are at most $B$
for every $j<n$, the stated doubled-word condition implies the target-stage configuration has the specified termination, register bound, and acceptance semantics
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, let $K(j)$ be a proposition for each
natural number $j$, and let $σ$ be a register configuration whose nine register values
are all at most $B$. Suppose the source register is $0$, the scratch register is $0$,
and $p+2n+2\le B$. If for every $j<n$, whenever the segment of $x$ beginning at $p$
consists of the binary word for $j$ with each bit repeated twice followed by the
separator $01$, the fixed program started at its next stage with source register $j$,
pointer $p+2|\mathrm{bits}(j)|+2$, and scratch register $0$ terminates within the
register bound and accepts exactly when $K(j)$ holds, then starting at the
existential-search stage with configuration $σ$ terminates within the register bound and
accepts exactly when there exists $j<n$ for which that doubled-block condition and
$K(j)$ both hold.
